status_summary: The one operative ICTS rule, the BIS connected vehicles rule issued 2025-01-14 before the period tracked, took effect on 2025-03-17 and is being administered: BIS issued General Authorization 1 for limited use cases on 2025-06-10, amended General Authorization 2 on 2025-11-19, and on 2026-06-18 amended General Authorization 1 and issued General Authorization 3, which lets suppliers not otherwise eligible for a specific authorization apply to an approved supplier registry; the registry itself is not yet posted. These authorizations appear on the BIS site; a Federal Register query found no BIS ICTS document after the January 2025 rule. The national emergency under Executive Order 13873 that supports the authority was continued by presidential notices dated 2025-05-09 and 2026-05-11. The drone (UAS) rulemaking remains at the advance notice published 2025-01-03, and no new ICTS determination or rule in another sector was found.

timeline.event: The BIS connected vehicles ICTS rule takes effect, per the BIS program page (issued 2025-01-14 and published 2025-01-16, before the period tracked); sales prohibitions apply from model year 2027 and hardware import prohibitions from model year 2030.
A presidential notice continues for one year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13873 on the ICTS supply chain (published 2025-05-14, 90 FR 20557).

BIS issues General Authorization 1 (limited use cases) under the connected vehicles rule, allowing manufacturers to import completed connected vehicles with covered technology without a specific authorization for short public-road testing, off-road display, testing or research, and temporary import for repair or competition, subject to recordkeeping and reporting conditions.
BIS amends General Authorization 2 (temporary importation) under the connected vehicles rule, per the BIS authorizations page.
A presidential notice again continues the Executive Order 13873 emergency (published 2026-05-13, 91 FR 27181).

BIS amends General Authorization 1 (limited use cases) and issues General Authorization 3, an approved supplier registry under which suppliers not otherwise eligible for a specific authorization may apply to list their vehicle connectivity hardware or covered software, so that listed items may be imported or sold without a specific authorization, subject to declarations of conformity, 10-year recordkeeping and BIS verification.

title: Fully implement the ICTS supply-chain authorities as a durable national security tool
uncertainties: General Authorizations 1 (as amended 2026-06-18) and 3 were read in full from the BIS site; General Authorization 2 and the archived versions were not opened, and the specific change made by the 2026-06-18 amendment to General Authorization 1 is not stated in the document. None of the authorizations was published in the Federal Register (a Federal Register API query for connected vehicles documents from BIS since 2025-01-01 returned only the January 2025 rule). Specific authorizations, the declarations of conformity process in practice and any enforcement were not described on the pages read. BIS opened a Section 232 investigation of drone imports on 2025-07-01, and the FCC added foreign drones to its Covered List (tracked in c28-03); these are other authorities, not ICTS rules. A pending Senate bill said to limit general authorizations was mentioned in an earlier draft without a source and was not verified. The connected vehicles rule text itself was not read; its issue, effective and compliance dates come from the BIS program page.
